expected_approaches.summary: Maintain unresolved indices whose temperatures decrease from stack bottom to top; resolve them when a warmer day arrives.
key_invariants: Every stacked index has no known warmer day yet.
Stack temperatures are nonincreasing, so a new warmer value resolves a suffix.
tradeoffs: Stores indices because the answer requires distances.
common_implementation_variants: reverse scan with a decreasing stack

alternative_approaches.summary: Scan backward while tracking nearest future positions for each temperature in the bounded domain.
alternative_approaches.applicability: Only when the temperature domain remains small and fixed.
assumptions: Temperature values are bounded by the stated range.
key_invariants: The stored position for each temperature is its nearest occurrence to the right.
tradeoffs: Uses domain-specific knowledge rather than general monotonic-stack reasoning.
common_failure_modes: using it without a bounded domain

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: vector<int> dailyTemperatures(vector<int> temperatures){ vector<int> out(temperatures.size()); vector<int> stack; for(int i=0;i<(int)temperatures.size();i++){while(!stack.empty()&&temperatures[i]>temperatures[stack.back()]){int j=stack.back();stack.pop_back();out[j]=i-j;} stack.push_back(i);} return out; } };

class Solution { public int[] dailyTemperatures(int[] temperatures){ int[] out=new int[temperatures.length]; java.util.Deque<Integer> stack=new java.util.ArrayDeque<>(); for(int i=0;i<temperatures.length;i++){while(!stack.isEmpty()&&temperatures[i]>temperatures[stack.peek()]){int j=stack.pop();out[j]=i-j;}stack.push(i);}return out;} }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: Each stack index awaits its first warmer day and stack temperatures remain nonincreasing.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: An index enters and leaves the stack at most once.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Equal temperatures do not resolve a strictly warmer query.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Leave indices with no later warmer day at zero.

counterexamples.purpose: One warm day can resolve multiple earlier indices.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: The bounded-domain alternative loses its fixed-range advantage.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend what every stacked index means.

expected_good_signals: each entry awaits its first warmer day
weak_or_misconception_signals: cannot state what a stack element represents
sample_phrasings: What does an index on your stack mean at this moment?
Should equal temperatures resolve each other here?

weak_or_misconception_signals: treats the while loop as automatically quadratic
sample_phrasings: Why can the total number of pops not exceed the number of days?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on the unresolved-index invariant and strict comparison.

reference_reasoning: The monotonic-stack approach is a strong prior, but other correct approaches should be evaluated on their own reasoning and constraints.
